newsitem.title: USA: Lockheed tops U.S. defense contractors.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed tops U.S. defense contractors.

text.p: Aerospace giant Lockheed Martin Corp. last year again led all U.S. defense contractors with $12 billion in prime military contract awards, the Defense Department said on Friday.

In an annual list of firms ranked by prime contracting funds, Lockheed led in fiscal 1996 for the second consecutive year. It was followed by McDonnell Douglas Corp. with $9.9 billion in contracts, General Motors Corp. with $3.2 billion, Raytheon Co. with $3 billion and General Dynamics Corp. with $2.7 billion.

Rounding out the top 10 firms were Northrop Grumman Corp and United Technologies Corp at $2.6 billion each, Boeing Co. and Litton Industries Inc. at $1.7 billion each, and General Electric Co. with $1.5 billion.
The merger of Lockheed and Martin Marietta in 1995 formed by far the nation's biggest defense contractor, but the proposed merger of McDonnell Douglas and Boeing poses a challenge to that standing.

Lockheed, which had $10.5 billion in prime contract awards in fiscal 1995, builds a wide range of weaponary from the F-16 fighter jet to missiles, helicopters and electronics and communications equipment.
McDonnell Douglas was second on the list for the second concecutive year, while General Motors vaulted to third on the 1996 list from fourth the previous year.
